name: Fix a Deployment that won't go Ready
objective: CKAD › Application Design and Build + Observability. Drill EVERY pod-design corner harder than the exam: classic vs native sidecars, init ordering, all three probe types and handlers, lifecycle hooks + graceful shutdown, full securityContext hardening, QoS classes, the Downward API, and a no-hint diagnose-and-fix. Graded exactly, per requirement.

questions.title: Diagnose & fix: a Deployment that won't go Ready
questions.teach:
To diagnose a pod that's `Running` but never `Ready`, run `kubectl describe pod

` and read **Events** — that's almost always a **readiness probe** pointed at the wrong port/path, so it never answers. Compare the probe target to the port the container actually serves. **Gotcha:** fix the **Deployment** (its pod template), not the pod — then confirm with `kubectl rollout status`.
questions.prompt:
Deployment `diag` in `pod-design` has 1 replica but it **never becomes Ready** (`kubectl -n pod-design get deploy diag` shows `0/1`). Diagnose the fault and fix it so the Deployment reports an available replica. Don't delete and rebuild from scratch — find and fix what's wrong.

Target: Deployment `diag` has at least 1 available replica.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n pod-design describe pod -l app=diag` → the readiness probe is failing. Compare the probe's port to the port the container (`nginx:1.25`) actually serves on. Fix the Deployment's readiness probe (`kubectl -n pod-design edit deploy diag`), then watch `rollout status`.
questions.solution:
# The readiness probe targets port 8080, but nginx serves on 80.
kubectl -n pod-design patch deployment diag --type=json \
  -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/readinessProbe/httpGet/port","value":80}]'
kubectl -n pod-design rollout status deployment/diag

verification.description: Deployment diag has >=1 available replica (readiness fault fixed)
